key_insight: Stitching artifacts can quietly degrade generative microscopy outputs, and FID alone may miss harms that matter for downstream segmentation.
clinical_relevance: For biomedical image generation and domain adaptation workflows, artifact-free patch stitching is more important than perceptual scores alone when the output will support analysis tasks.
method: Compared cycleGAN models trained on cryo-electron microscopy volumes using 2D vs 3D patching.
Tested three stitching strategies to assess border artifacts during volume assembly.
Evaluated outputs with FID, perceptual quality checks, and downstream mitochondria segmentation; also tested orthogonal-direction ensembling.
evidence_signal: Across the abstract’s experiments, subtle stitching artifacts were not captured by FID but did affect segmentation performance, while 3D artifact-free stitching only slightly outperformed 2D despite higher compute cost.
watch_item: The modest gain from 3D models may not justify the extra computational burden, so implementation should prioritize artifact control and task-based evaluation over perceptual metrics alone.
paper_title: Stitching and dimensionality effects on large artificially generated volume datasets
